headline: Regional Access and Activity Planning in the Blue Ridge
reservation: The New River Valley consists of various state parks and national forest lands; while general access is open, specific campgrounds at Claytor Lake and river outfitter slots require independent reservations. Check Virginia State Parks for lodging availability and the Jefferson National Forest for specific trailhead status.

days.title: Highland Peaks and Academic Greens

stops.name: Hahn Horticulture Garden
stops.detail: Wander through the diverse plant collections on the Virginia Tech campus to see native Blue Ridge flora.

stops.name: Mountain Lake Biological Station Area
stops.detail: Explore the high-elevation trails near this historic site, known for its unique microclimate.

days.driving: Allow 30–45 minutes for local mountain roads; conditions vary.
days.note: Blacksburg can be very busy during university event weekends; check local calendars.

days.title: Cascades and River Limestone

stops.name: Cascades Falls
stops.detail: Hike the 4-mile loop to a 66-foot waterfall set within a dramatic stone amphitheater.

stops.name: New River Access Points
stops.detail: Observe the ancient limestone cliffs from the riverbanks or via a local guided paddling trip.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes to reach trailheads; conditions vary.
days.note: The Cascades trail can be slippery and wet; use caution on the lower creek-side path.

days.title: Rail Trails and Lakefront Relaxation

stops.name: New River Trail State Park
stops.detail: Cycle or walk a portion of this 57-mile linear park that follows a historic railroad bed along the water.

stops.name: Claytor Lake State Park
stops.detail: Visit the Howe House or utilize the lakefront trails for views of this significant regional waterway.

days.driving: Allow 40–50 minutes between the trail and the lake; conditions vary.
days.note: Bicycle rentals are seasonal; confirm availability with local providers before arrival.

intel.title: State Park Fees
intel.text: Daily parking fees apply at Claytor Lake and New River Trail access points. Ensure you have the correct payment method for the self-service kiosks at more remote trailheads.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Effects
intel.text: Cellular coverage is reliable in Blacksburg and Christiansburg but frequently drops in the gaps and along the river. Carry physical maps when exploring the Jefferson National Forest areas.

intel.title: Valley Hubs
intel.text: Fuel up in Christiansburg or Radford before heading toward the Cascades or the Blue Ridge Parkway. Options are sparse once you enter the national forest boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Runoff
intel.text: River activities are highly dependent on spring snowmelt and rainfall levels from the surrounding peaks. Consult local outfitters for current water safety and flow rate advisories.

intel.title: Linear Park Logistics
intel.text: The New River Trail is 57 miles long; plan your entry and exit points carefully as shuttle services are not always available. Most sections are crushed gravel suitable for hybrid bicycles.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at ROA and drive 64 minutes west to Christiansburg for major supply shopping before heading to your mountain lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads, though an SUV is recommended for forest service road access; check rental terms for gravel road usage.
plan.goldenHour: Overlooks along the Blue Ridge Parkway near Adney Gap offer expansive valley views, subject to local mountain mist.
